A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAAT/HumanML3D++ work, and all supplied pages, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Neither PDF contains an appendix. v4 references separate supplementary metric details unavailable here, but the supplied material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original TAAT benchmark results, zero-shot evaluations, dataset validation, an index-length ablation, and a user study.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and additionally reports dataset-filtering and prompt-design ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain LoRA fine-tuning of an LLM, VQ-VAE motion tokenization, and autoregressive Transformer generation conditioned on previous-action indices. Renaming action representations as instructions and rewriting the mathematical exposition do not establish a changed generation method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HumanML3D action texts and HumanML3D++ scene texts under the same retraining and zero-shot scenarios. The added filtering and prompt studies remain within this coverage; replacing an illustrative scene does not establish a new evaluation domain.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparator set remains TM2T, MDM, MLD, MotionDiffuse, and T2M-GPT. Qualitative comparisons retain MLD, MDM, and T2M-GPT, and the user study retains T2M-GPT. The new unfiltered TAAT row is an ablation.

E3.justification: v3 defines Mean Hit Distance as the average of per-input minimum distances. v4 Section 5 instead aggregates qualifying-hit distances, using a minimum-distance fallback when no response hits, substantially changing a central evaluation metric. v4 also changes the stated AdamW beta1 from 0.5 to 0.9 and introduces filtering and prompt-feature controls. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 substantially broadens ablation coverage from motion continuity to dataset construction: Table 3 tests removing filtering, and Table 6 tests verb restrictions, quantity requirements, examples, and causality in prompts. The existing index-length analysis is retained as Figure 7. The scene-text case study also changes from an approaching motorcycle to a sunset scene.

E5.justification: The user-study error-bar whiskers in v3 Figure 5 disappear in v4 Figure 6, although the percentages remain unchanged. Their statistical meaning was not specified in v3. Benchmark plus/minus reporting is retained, with no newly stated seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: The matched main benchmark scores and user-study percentages are retained. v4 adds an unfiltered TAAT result with Hit Accuracy 78.6, FID 0.420, and Mean Hit Distance 1.195, plus prompt-quality results including accuracy 98.4 and score 5.00 for the full prompt. v3's 94% dataset-validation finding disappears. These are added or removed findings, not evidence of a same-setting performance improvement over v3.

T1.justification: v4 Equation 9 changes the mathematical meaning of Mean Hit Distance from averaging per-input minima to aggregating qualifying responses with fallback minima. This is a substantive redefinition of a proposed central metric. v4 also adds an LLM log-likelihood expression described as minimized, conflicting with its retained cross-entropy formulation, and removes v3's explicit VQ-VAE loss equations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the arbitrary-text motion task, HumanML3D++, the think-and-act framework, and evaluation accommodating multiple plausible motions. The new title and contribution list emphasize the task and 'multi-solution' terminology without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations that filtering removes irrelevant or noisy samples and that examples and verb restrictions are particularly important for prompt quality. It also identifies excessive requested scene descriptions as a source of inappropriate outputs. Existing interpretations concerning generalization, motion diversity, and index-length tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly documents automatic length/format checks and three-rater consensus for data validation. It omits v3's verbatim generation prompt, explicit VQ-VAE loss and EMA/code-reset descriptions, and 196-frame maximum-length disclosure. Most architecture sizes and training schedules remain. Both versions promise future resource release rather than provide access.

R1.justification: The new Extended Text to Motion Generation subsection substantially expands positioning against human-scene, human-object, and multi-person generation, citing works including GenZI, InterDiff, InterGen, and Inter-X. It argues for the flexibility of textual scene descriptions relative to additional 3D conditioning. This extends v3's primarily conventional text-to-motion comparison.

P1.justification: v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, dataset construction, and method exposition. It changes the title and author block, creates a standalone Metrics section, reorganizes user-study and ablation subsections, and systematically shifts terminology toward action instructions and multi-solution generation.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the task, dataset, and pipeline diagrams; adds dataset-distribution charts; merges the retraining and zero-shot tables; and separates action-text and scene-text visualizations. It converts the index-length table into a plot and redesigns the user-study chart. These are extensive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new filtering and prompt ablations strengthen support for dataset construction, while expanded related work and reorganized figures improve context and readability. However, v4 changes Mean Hit Distance while retaining its scores, and its Hit Accuracy prose contradicts Equation 7 about the threshold direction. It also removes user-study error bars and some reproducibility details. The unresolved implications for a central evaluation contribution prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
